APPENDIX
GLOSSARY OF TERMS RELATING

A
TO PURSE SEINES

Purse Seirte -A long wall of webbing without prominent bunt or bag that is with very little fullness and with the webbing hanging nearly straight down between the float and head lines. The essential feature of the net is the pursing by pulling a purse line, which is threaded through rings, along the bottom of the net.

rings, the hauling of which effects the closing of the net.
Breast Line -

A purse seine has generally three broad divisions, namely, main body, wing and bunt, each of which cannot be demarcated separately.
Ma& Body Bunt -The

This is the float line carried beyond the upper corner of the net to form a loop spliced heavily or lashed at its base, then extended down the end of webbing to the lower corner of the net. Frequently it is extended back along the lead line.
Bridles

4

The portion which forms the bulk of the net and lies in between the wing and the bunt. end which is shot first and hauled up the catch is accumulated for brailing and is of stronger webbing. It is a small portion net, say one or two panels, and is shorter in than the other panels.

Haul-in bridles (ski$ end bridle and line, and wing end bridle and line) - Pairs ~of ropes

when made of the depth

attached to the head rope and foot rope of the bunt and wing ends forming a triangle and connected to the skiff and boat respectively by single lines.
bridle -The rope connecting each purse ring with the foot rope either one or if two forming a triangle, in the latter case the apex angle is less than 60". This enables easy and effective pursing. Ring

b)

Wing - The end of the net which is shot last and hauled up first. Selvedge -

A definite number of rows of meshes at the upper and lower borders and at extremities of the webbing fabricated with twines thicker than those of the main webbing.

Rings attached to the foot rope at equal intervals according to the length of the net.
Purse Rings Lifting L&e -

Head Rope -

The rope or line to which the upper edge of the net is finally attached. rope or line to which the lower edge of the net is attached. The line attached to head rope through which the floats are threaded in.

The line used for lifting a group of floats of limited number while in operation if required and during hauling. Brail A long-handled dip net.

Foot Rope -The .Float Litie -

Dipping or landing of fish out of the net into the fishing boat. The term is also used for landing of fish from the boat to the cannery or the jetty.
Brailing Ski$-- A small boat usually 6 to 8 m long, operated along with a purse seiner to help in pursing the corks and to hold up the outer side of the landing bag for brailing the catch.

Lead Line -The line attached to the foot rope through which the sinkers are threaded in.

Purse Line -The

line passing through

the purse
